candidates.summary: Jessica's seal noise; John guesses 'That is me having sex'; both break down laughing; walrus debate; 'I'm going to remember this moment'
candidates.reason: Strong immediate hook (odd noise + card visible to viewer), unexpected guess, genuine laughter as payoff; self-contained in 25 s. Mild sexual innuendo noted.

candidates.summary: Jessica tastes salt licorice ('hard no'), warns John not to; he tries anyway: 'Epsom salt bath in your mouth', 'abomination of a candy'
candidates.reason: Clear setup -> warning -> he does it anyway -> vivid reactions; strong quotable lines.

candidates.summary: Cup-flip game: John announces 'I got a strategy', loses 1 vs 25, 'I miscalculated my efficiencies'
candidates.reason: Setup/payoff (confident strategy -> 1-25 loss) is easy to follow and visual; score graphic shows the result.

candidates.summary: Mouth-chopstick hoop game: chaos, 'What the fudge and mustard', John ends on 0 vs Jessica 5, claw-machine comparison
candidates.reason: Visually unusual physical comedy; distinct from the cup game (different action, John's own commentary).

candidates.summary: Movie-quote quiz (Taxi Driver, Terminator, Braveheart, Star Wars...)
candidates.reason: Score 69: long and list-like, no single payoff; quotes are shown as source graphics, little to add editorially.

candidates.summary: Card 'The time is now (John's WWE theme)' during the noise game
candidates.reason: Score 68: payoff unclear and key line is uncertain in the ASR ('wrestling wife/life?') - risk of misquoting.

candidates.summary: Snoring noise; 'that's my poor wife'
candidates.reason: Score 64: too slight on its own; overlaps the seal clip's game.

candidates.summary: Snack tastings: celery/peanut butter, pickles, Percy Pigs
candidates.reason: Score 53: pleasant but no conflict or payoff.

candidates.summary: Wrap-up and 'I'm gonna beat you... physical violence' banter
candidates.reason: Score 54: relies on context, weak ending; contains end-screen.

candidates.summary: Show intro/trailer
candidates.reason: Score 47: produced trailer graphics, no moment of its own.

candidates.summary: US went from >90% of world uranium enrichment to <1%; Russia controls ~44%; 'one of America's biggest adversaries controls the fuel behind our grid'
candidates.reason: Concrete, surprising statistic with a clear stakes payoff; works standalone.

candidates.summary: Opening question 'what if the real nuclear threat is that we no longer control it?' + closing answer 'The danger was never the technology...'
candidates.reason: Strongest hook of the video; pairs the opening question with Jake's own closing answer (same speaker, same thesis) so the clip has a payoff. Absorbs the separate closing-statement candidate to avoid two clips on the same point.

candidates.summary: Kentucky Governor Andy Beshear: 'something I never thought I'd say - Jake Paul, welcome to Paducah'; 'largest economic investment in the history of Western Kentucky'
candidates.reason: Unexpected, funny opening line from a governor; clear payoff (record investment).

candidates.summary: 'Biggest misconception: nuclear is dangerous - it's the cleanest and safest energy'; Energy Secretary Chris Wright on falling electricity costs
candidates.reason: Contrarian claim as hook, backed by a cabinet secretary; distinct topic (safety/cost). Claims are presented as the speakers' statements.

candidates.summary: 'America gave this away once, and we're not doing it again... the danger is letting someone else control it'
candidates.reason: Score 77 but same thesis as cand-no-longer-control-it; used as that clip's payoff instead of a separate, repetitive clip.

candidates.summary: Paducah used 10% of all US electricity at one point; 3 gigawatts; shut down 2013
candidates.reason: Score 74: striking fact but the payoff (economics, shutdown) is flat; overlaps the 90%->1% clip.

candidates.summary: Uranium enrichment explained with 1,000 marbles
candidates.reason: Score 70: clear but educational, weak hook.

candidates.summary: Paducah built for WWII TNT, then nuclear
candidates.reason: Score 64: background history, no payoff.

candidates.summary: 'Jake, why are you here?' - Anti Fund and reindustrialization
candidates.reason: Score 64: mostly fund promotion.

candidates.summary: Rail yard tour; 'I feel like I'm in Atlas Shrugged'
candidates.reason: Score 55: niche reference, little payoff.
